chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn al-Sindi from Hammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Yusuf from his father, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Ju'hani came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said: O Messenger of Allah, I have camels, sheep, a group of people, and a group of servants. I wish for you to command me regarding a night in which I enter [the mosque] and attend the prayer, and that is in the month of Ramadan. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) called him and whispered to him in his ear. So the Ju'hani, when it was the night of the twenty-third, would enter with his camels, his sheep, and his family to his place.'

key_terms.الْجُهَنِيّ: A member of the Ju'ham tribe, the subject of the narration
key_terms.عَمَلَةً: A group of servants or workers
key_terms.غِلْمَةً: A group or company of people

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet (SAWW) whisper to Al-Ju'hani regarding entering the mosque with livestock in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the flexibility of Ramadan worship practices in early Islamic society, where livestock owners could bring their herds into the mosque precincts to combine trade care with devotion. The Prophet’s whispered instruction likely specified the night of the 23rd, a date of significant importance in Shia tradition for the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr), emphasizing the spiritual weight of this specific night. It illustrates the practical integration of daily livelihood with religious observance during the holy month.
